answer: Submissions that land within 210 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The sable detector writes to quill, and orchard reveals every merge. A farm scripting its whole swarm fires them together, thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 205 aliases out burns the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 26 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
